name: Noon Chai
steps: Put the tea leaves and cracked cardamom in a deep stainless-steel pan with 500 ml of the measured water. Reserve the remaining 300 ml water in the refrigerator until cold.
Bring to a boil and add exactly the measured baking soda. Simmer uncovered for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tea is concentrated and reddish-brown; do not let the pan dry out.
Add the reserved cold water. Keep the pan on low heat and repeatedly lift and pour the tea back with a ladle for 5 minutes, keeping the ladle close to the pan to avoid splashes.
Strain the concentrate into a clean pan, add the milk and salt, and simmer for 5–7 minutes. The colour should soften to dusty pink or pinkish tan; its shade depends on the tea leaves.
Slice the almonds finely. Divide the hot salted tea among four cups and scatter the almonds over each; serve without sugar for this savoury version.
tips: Use tea sold for noon chai. Do not add extra baking soda to force a brighter pink: it makes the tea unpleasantly alkaline.
notes: Four cups of traditional salted tea, not a sweet pink dessert drink. Contains milk, almonds and caffeine.
